questions.q: How does the passage portray Brunel's career overall?
options: As brilliant and visionary but marked by frequent setbacks
As a steady run of commercial triumphs that made him wealthy
As confined to railways and rarely noticed outside Britain
As overshadowed throughout life by his famous father Marc
questions.explain: He was a great figure of the Industrial Revolution but his career was marred by continual setbacks.

questions.q: What gauge did Brunel choose for the GWR?
options: An atmospheric gauge
7 ft 1/4 in broad gauge
A narrow gauge
Standard gauge
questions.explain: He chose broad gauge of 7 ft 1/4 in, which became problematic.

questions.q: Why was Brunel sent to study under Breguet in Paris?
options: Breguet was his mother's cousin and offered a paid apprenticeship
Foreigners were barred from École Polytechnique, and Britain had no degrees
He failed the entrance examination for the Henri Quatre College in Caen
His father was held in a Paris debtors' prison and needed his help
questions.explain: He was deemed ineligible for École Polytechnique and chose to study under the clockmaker Breguet.

questions.q: What happened to Marc Brunel in 1821?
options: He fled to Russia to work for Alexander I after losing his fortune
He was knighted by the Duke of Wellington for his block-making machinery
He was jailed for debt, then freed when the Chancellor paid it on condition he stay in Britain
His sawmill burned down and the government refused to pay for his army boot order
questions.explain: He was jailed in King's Bench Prison, then released after Wellington's warning led to £5,000 being issued.

questions.q: What does the passage imply about Brunel's ships?
options: They were designed by John Scott Russell
They were often too far ahead of their time to succeed commercially
They all sank
They were commercially the most profitable of the era
questions.explain: His maritime works were remembered as too far ahead of their time to see success.
